Temporarily disables Wi-Fi, captures up to 24 scheduled mobile-radio snapshots over two minutes, then restores Wi-Fi. The report excludes phone numbers, IMSI, and ICCID. It includes tower cell IDs and radio details, which can reveal approximate location; review it before sharing publicly.

For two minutes, opens every supported Android-side LTE/NR gate, requests Automatic bands where supported, keeps the data connection active with small connectivity checks, and captures the full field-test report. Previous settings are restored automatically.

Experimental test only. It cannot lower tower-controlled attach thresholds or create signal. It temporarily changes radio policy, uses a small amount of mobile data, and may increase battery use. Do not use during an emergency call.

Keep the phone near the target site and mobile data enabled. The app will temporarily open supported LTE/NR gates and generate small network requests for two minutes, then restore the captured settings even if you stop the test.

New here? Read the safe workflow before changing IMS, radio profiles, or bands.
Follow the path for your selected access mode. Start with NSA and Automatic bands for Sri Lankan networks, then confirm the result in Monitor or Field Test.

1. On Home, choose Root and grant superuser access in your root manager.

2. Open Controls → Band selection & LTE+. Keep bands on Automatic, select Force NSA, and tap Force all local 5G gates.

3. On Setup, validate and install the regional modem patch, then reboot. KernelSU uses a single-file boot mount and needs no metamodule. If an old KernelSU overlay is inactive, use Revalidate for this firmware to migrate it. Magisk and APatch use their overlays.

4. Near a known 5G site, enable mobile data and check Monitor or the standard Field Test for EN-DC/NR attachment. Use SA only when the carrier offers SA.

After a Pixel firmware update, remove the old regional patch before updating, reboot, then validate and install a fresh patch for the new baseband. Root cannot create tower coverage or bypass carrier/SIM authorization.

1. Start the separate Shizuku app, choose Shizuku on Home, and grant Pixel IMS 5G permission.

2. Open Controls → Band selection & LTE+. Keep bands on Automatic and select Force NSA. Easy Mode can open VoLTE, LTE+, LTE+NR, and carrier aggregation together.

3. Tap Apply Shizuku regional profile. The app opens every reversible Android-side user/carrier NR gate it can access and verifies the effective result.

4. Test near a known 5G site with mobile data enabled. Use Monitor or Field Test to check NR Available, EN-DC Available, NR state, LTE anchor, and any reported modem limitation.

Shizuku cannot replace Tensor cfg.db or modify the vendor modem profile. If every Android-side gate is open but EN-DC remains rejected, regional 5G may still require the Root/Magisk modem compatibility patch.

Choose Root or Shizuku, confirm the privileged service and SIM are detected, then check IMS registration for each SIM. Use FIX only when IMS is unavailable and you want Google/carrier defaults restored.

Open IMS & 5G controls for VoLTE, VoWiFi, VoNR and NSA/SA settings. Open Band selection & LTE+ for Easy Mode, radio preference, carrier aggregation and advanced bands. Keep Automatic bands unless you know your carrier’s deployed bands.

Opening Monitor temporarily disables Wi-Fi so readings and traffic stay on the mobile-radio path; Wi-Fi is restored when the page closes. VoWiFi/IWLAN cannot be tested during this isolated session. Root exposes deeper phone-process evidence; Shizuku pages clearly mark unavailable privileged data.

Both test modes temporarily disable Wi-Fi and restore its previous state afterward. Standard mode leaves radio policy unchanged. Aggressive mode temporarily opens supported LTE/NR gates and sends small mobile-data checks, then rolls back. Share the generated report when reporting a device or carrier problem.

If a manual band or SA-only setting removes service, use Undo when offered. The power icon restores all app-managed SIM settings and reboots. Remove the root regional modem patch before a firmware update, then validate it again afterward.

Pixel IMS 5G cannot amplify RF signal, create tower coverage, lower network-controlled attach thresholds, bypass subscriber authorization, or guarantee 5G/VoWiFi. Root-only modem changes remain unavailable through Shizuku.
IWLAN is the IMS-over-Wi-Fi transport, not cellular band 1800. This monitor shows Wi-Fi frequency, IMS transport, and the LTE/NR anchor separately.

Root Force snapshots the current state, removes band restrictions, enables NSA + SA in CarrierConfig, opens every readable allowed-network reason, enables IMS debug gates, and restarts IMS. It does not write modem NV/EFS. Device-specific NV profiles must match the exact Pixel model and baseband.

Experimental systemless Tensor modem patch. It copies this firmware’s own cfg.db, validates the SQLite schema and integrity, and maps only wildcard/PTCRB carrier entries to the firmware’s permissive profile. It does not fake the SIM country, registered PLMN, or Wi-Fi regulatory country.

KernelSU uses a verified, read-only boot bind of cfg.db and needs no metamodule. Magisk and APatch use their systemless overlay. A reboot is required. Before a firmware update, remove this patch and reboot; afterward validate a fresh copy. The installer refuses unknown layouts. A local modem profile cannot bypass carrier authentication, subscriber entitlement, tower configuration or RF limits.
Root mode with Magisk, KernelSU or APatch is required. This operation is unavailable through Shizuku.

Applies every reversible Android-side regional gate available to the Shizuku shell: LTE + NR network policy, NSA + SA CarrierConfig, VoLTE, VoWiFi, VoNR, LTE+ and IMS visibility. It requests Automatic bands where the modem API supports it, then reads the effective regional gates back.
Android-side Shizuku gates are open. Test near the 5G site.
Android-side Shizuku gates are open. Automatic band reset is unavailable on this modem, so the existing band selection was left unchanged.

%1$s detected. The Shizuku method cannot honestly guarantee regional 5G without modifying the vendor modem configuration. It can open Android-side gates, but it cannot replace Tensor cfg.db or force the network to expose EN-DC.

Important: this is not the Tensor cfg.db modem patch that made 5G work in the root comparison. Android 17 blocks UID 2000 from installing a vendor/Magisk overlay. If the modem profile still rejects EN-DC after these gates pass, the same modem fix still requires root.

The app will validate and stage a patched carrier database. On KernelSU, a boot script binds only cfg.db as read-only; no metamodule or directory overlay is used. On Magisk and APatch, the manager mounts the overlay. Reboot to activate. If service becomes unstable, disable this module in your root manager and reboot.
Magisk will remove the systemless overlay during the next reboot and restore the stock firmware database.

RSRP: useful signal strength. Less negative is stronger. RSRQ: signal quality; less negative is usually better. SINR: signal clarity; higher is better. RSSI: total received power including noise. CQI: radio quality used to select coding, not a speed score. EARFCN / NR-ARFCN: the exact LTE / 5G channel. PCI: a reusable radio cell identity, not a unique tower ID. TAC: the tracking area used for mobility and paging. Cell ID: the network\'s cell identifier. eNB / sector is derived from the LTE cell ID. Bandwidth: radio spectrum width, not download speed. Timing advance: timing compensation, not an accurate tower distance. Not reported: the phone supplied no valid value; it does not mean zero.
No changes recorded in this session.
Attach trace, physical channels and carrier settings
This carrier is no longer reported in the current sample. These are its last available measurements.
4G+ combines radio carriers. NSA 5G adds a 5G link alongside a 4G anchor; SA connects directly to 5G. Availability alone does not establish an active 5G link.
Strength measures useful radio signal. Clarity measures how well it stands out from interference. A strong signal can still be noisy.
Live readings for %1$s. Missing values mean the modem did not expose them; they are not zero.
Measured cell, not confirmed as part of this SIM\'s active carrier combination.
Current physical-channel report for this SIM slot. Registration state determines whether 5G is counted as connected; conflicting observations are retained for diagnosis.
Whether the phone is registered for mobile service.
The data access technology reported by the selected SIM\'s registration state.
This distinguishes NR availability from an active 5G secondary connection.
The channel reported by ServiceState for the selected SIM.
FDD separates upload and download by frequency; TDD separates them by time.
Services advertised by the current packet-service registration. These do not guarantee IMS provisioning.
Extra LTE carriers can increase capacity. Android sometimes confirms CA without exposing each extra carrier.
ServiceState may retain this list between radio updates. Current identified component widths are shown in the carrier section above.
Connected NR state or serving NR evidence establishes 5G. A status-bar icon alone does not.
The network advertises NR availability. This does not mean a 5G carrier is connected.
The network advertises the ability to combine LTE and NR. This is a capability, not an active attachment.
Whether the network reports a restriction on LTE/NR dual connectivity.
IMS provides calling services. IWLAN means Wi-Fi calling; LTE/NR means cellular IMS.
Whether Android reports registration on a roaming network.
The country and operator identifiers of the serving network.
A network rejection code when reported. Zero normally means no rejection; missing is not a rejection.
Whether registration reports that the phone is searching for service.
Whether Android reports a satellite or other non-terrestrial connection.
Role reported by the current physical channel for this SIM slot.
Role based on this SIM\'s serving-cell evidence.
LTE B-number or 5G n-number. Multiple carriers can use the same band on different channels.
The exact radio channel number distinguishes two carriers on the same band.
Physical Cell Identity helps distinguish radio cells; it is not a unique tower ID.
Width of this receiving carrier, not your measured download speed.
Channel used to send data to the network.
Width of this carrier\'s upload channel.
The receiving frequency exposed by the physical-channel report.
The sending frequency exposed by the physical-channel report.
The modem has not exposed measurements for this serving carrier.
MCC-MNC identifies the cell\'s country and operator.
Reference-signal strength. Less negative is stronger; −90 dBm is stronger than −110 dBm.
Reference-signal quality, influenced by interference and loading. Less negative is generally better.
Useful signal compared with interference and noise. Higher is clearer.
Total received power, including interference; different from reference-signal strength.
Channel Quality Indicator helps the network select modulation and coding; not a speed measurement.
Android\'s coarse signal level. The detailed measurements provide more context.
EARFCN for LTE or NR-ARFCN for 5G identifies the radio channel.
Frequency reported or calculated from the standardized channel mapping.
Physical Cell Identity is reused across the network, so is not a unique site identifier.
Tracking Area Code groups cells for mobility and paging.
LTE cell identity or 5G NCI. Identifies a cell, not an accurate map location.
Derived from LTE cell identity using the conventional 8-bit sector split; not a GPS location.
Width of this carrier. CA can combine several separate widths.
Radio timing compensation; not a reliable direct distance to the tower.
Bands for this measured cell; this list alone does not prove multiple CA carriers.
Primary handles signaling and possibly data; secondary supports data. Nearby cells are not automatically serving cells.
5G CSI signal clarity relative to interference and noise.
Table used to interpret the 5G channel quality report.
Per-resource quality values supplied by the modem.
Root mode reads Android’s active PhysicalChannelConfig list: primary/secondary status, RAT, band, PCI, channel, bandwidth, and frequency. Entries cover all active modems.
Root required. Shizuku cannot read READ_PRECISE_PHONE_STATE physical-channel internals on current Tensor Pixel builds.
Carrier aggregation is confirmed when at least one SecondaryServing LTE channel appears. NSA is confirmed only when an NR SecondaryServing channel or NR connected state appears.
Root snapshot available; direct phone-process hook is not used
Shizuku exposes framework registration state only; root required for internals

One or more Android allowed-network reasons exclude NR.
The network registration marks dual-connectivity NR as restricted.
NR is advertised/eligible, but this LTE registration reports EN-DC unavailable. This matches the captured Dialog B41 case: no NSA SCG can be formed on the current anchor.
The current registration does not advertise NR availability.
EN-DC is available but no SCG is connected. Generate root evidence during data traffic to identify a rejection or radio failure.
The framework has not exposed enough state to determine the attach failure.
Android does not expose the RRC SCG request/reject cause through public APIs. A network rejection is only reported when root radio evidence contains one.
Not available in Shizuku mode. Switch the app to Root mode to read sanitized TelephonyRegistry, phone-service, and radio-log evidence.
Effective per-SIM values are compared with Android’s built-in defaults. Carrier defaults are not automatically “better”; green means the effective value leaves that feature gate open.

“Configured” is not the same as connected. NSA also requires an LTE anchor advertising EN-DC and successful network SCG admission. VoNR additionally requires SA registration, IMS provisioning, and carrier support.
The radio did not answer. Root or Shizuku has to be connected to read cell information.
Radio log capture in Field Test

A new root-only option saves the vendor RIL logs (sit-ril), the modem\'s capability logs, the radio log buffer and telephony state to a ZIP in Downloads, with a Share button. It is read-only and never changes a setting.
The capture shows the modem\'s EN-DC capability events with their cause codes and decodes each capability log into the LTE and 5G band combinations the phone offered the network.
IMSI, ICCID, IMEI, phone numbers and IP addresses are masked before anything leaves the app. Binary RIL files that cannot be redacted are skipped while redaction is on.
Pixel 10 Pro XL 5G is still under investigation
This release adds the tool to diagnose it; it does not fix the Pixel 10 Pro XL staying on LTE where other phones get 5G.

The 5G and EN-DC timeline now lists only real changes: NR advertised and EN-DC available per SIM with the serving channel, 5G state transitions and status-bar 5G changes. Ordinary registration lines no longer appear as false events.
Last boot and capability log timing
The capture shows when the phone last booted and marks each modem capability log as at, since or before the last boot, so a capability written during startup is easy to spot.
Pixel 10 Pro XL 5G is still under investigation
This release improves the diagnostic capture; it does not fix the Pixel 10 Pro XL staying on LTE where other phones get 5G.
A completely new Home and Network design with translucent glass panels, clear typography and plain-language explanations, in light and dark.
Live carrier aggregation, in plain sight

Network shows every current LTE CA carrier with its own band, channel, PCI, bandwidth and signal readings. Totals follow the carriers reported in each sample, so 3 to 2 to 1 carriers update immediately; Android\'s retained summary is labelled separately.
5G anchor and NR status that tells the truth

Separates the LTE anchor, an active 5G carrier and nearby cells. When the network advertises 5G but the modem reports EN-DC unavailable, the monitor says 5G advertised, LTE only, instead of implying a 5G connection.
Fixes the raw Android service-state text and the numeric 413-02 title; carriers show as Dialog, SLT-MOBITEL and so on.
Home now holds access, enabled settings and modem compatibility. Live connection, signal and CA readings live on Network.
More Tensor Pixels for the modem patch
Adds Pixel 8a, Pixel 9a, Pixel 10 and Pixel 10a to the validated device list. The installer still validates each phone\'s own modem database first.
Pixel 10 Pro XL 5G is still under investigation
The modem patch is active and the phone advertises n78 capability, but some Pixel 10 Pro XL users still stay on LTE where other phones get 5G. This release does not fix that yet.
Includes the working 2.2.5 root startup, queued permission requests and Binder identity fixes. KernelSU mounts only cfg.db at boot without a metamodule; Magisk keeps its existing module path.
Preserves read-only single-file mounting, hash and SELinux checks, rollback on failure, and clear active or stale patch status after firmware updates.
Includes the 2.2.1 fix distinguishing failed callback registration from successful registration with no events. Timed polling remains the primary evidence when callbacks are unavailable.
Includes the 2.2.1 fix separating missing serving cells, conflicting CellInfo and unmatched device-global physical channels, without treating another SIM\'s evidence as selected-SIM proof.
The regional modem patch now mounts only cfg.db at boot through KernelSU\'s native module support. No directory overlay or mounting metamodule is required.
The boot script verifies the source and target, remounts the bind read-only, records its status, and rolls back instead of leaving a partial mount when validation fails.
Clearer patch state after firmware updates
Setup now distinguishes an active patch from a staged or stale module and offers Revalidate when the modem database must be rebuilt for the current firmware.
A failed callback registration is no longer described as successful. Timed polling remains the primary evidence when callbacks are unavailable.

Reports distinguish missing serving-cell observations, conflicting CellInfo, and unmatched device-global physical channels. An unrelated physical-channel snapshot no longer implies a CellInfo conflict.

Panels are now translucent glass over a lit background, with a specular rim and highlight. The floating tab bar has a glass lens that slides between tabs. A new button in the top bar switches between System, Light and Dark.
The modem patch leads Home for root users
As soon as root is granted, the 5G regional modem patch is the first card on Setup, with its prerequisites checked and one install button. Once active it shrinks to a single line.
The regional modem patch now installs with KernelSU (with a mounting metamodule such as mountify) and APatch, not only Magisk.
An opt-in switch on SIM Config saves your changes and reapplies them once Shizuku is running after a reboot.
No more crash when applying a setting on Android 17
Android 17 QPR2 changed a system call the app made after every change, which crashed the app even though the setting had applied. That call is now handled safely.
Settings no longer report \'did not accept\' by mistake
The app checked the result before Android had finished applying it. It now waits for the change to land.
Modem patch installs on Android 15 builds that refused it
The installer failed with \'Unable to find app for caller\' when opening the modem database as root. Failures are now shown on the card instead of doing nothing.
Setup no longer reports 5G as failing while the phone is on NSA 5G.
The modem patch always asks first
Every install, from any screen, now goes through the confirmation dialog.
The app opens on the answer
A new Setup screen tells you whether 5G is working on this SIM and, if it is not, which single thing is blocking it. No more hunting through twenty switches to find the one that matters.
Each failing check carries the action that addresses it: enable VoLTE, set NR to NSA and SA, enable VoNR, apply the Magisk modem patch, restart IMS, or open band selection.

There is no point telling you the modem refused EN-DC if VoLTE was never switched on. The last two checks are outcomes rather than settings — whether an NR cell is actually registered, and whether IMS registered.

2.0 shipped the glass panels far too faint to see. The design was ported from a web prototype that had a background blur behind every panel, which Android cannot do — so the panels now carry the contrast themselves.
Every individual carrier config switch is one tap away under Expert settings, and the previous overview screen is still there.
A new Network tab samples the radio every three seconds instead of taking one reading when you open a page. Serving cell, LTE anchor on NSA, and every neighbour cell in view, sorted by strength.
A rolling plot of the last ninety samples with min, mean and max. A dropout has a shape - a cliff is a handover, a slow slide is you walking away from the cell.
Handovers, band changes, NR leg up and down, service loss and sudden signal drops, each timestamped. Only real transitions are recorded, not every sample.
PCI, EARFCN and NR-ARFCN, TAC, cell ID, RSRQ, SINR, CSI-RSRP, CSI-SINR, RSSI, CQI, bandwidth and timing advance, all on one screen.

A new design: a lit navy ground with frosted panels, an animated swept-arc gauge for the headline reading, and Chakra Petch and JetBrains Mono shipping with the app so measurements are set in a real fixed-width face.
The attach trace, physical channels, registry event log and CarrierConfig diff are all still there, now one tap away under Deep diagnostics on the Network tab.

The violet and cyan glass theme is gone. The app now uses a neutral instrument palette: grey structure, one blue accent, and colour reserved for signal state so a green reading actually means something.
Band numbers, NRARFCN, PCI, signal measurements, and the event log now use a fixed-width face, so digits stay in their columns instead of shifting sideways as a live reading updates.
Settings rows no longer each float in their own card. Related controls are grouped into panels with dividers, so SIM Config reads as four decisions rather than twenty loose switches.
The floating rounded pill is now a flush bar with a hairline above it, and the bouncing icon animation is gone.
Signal colours are tuned separately for light and dark instead of sharing one value, so nothing is washed out on a white background.
The entrance animation on every page header has been removed. It delayed the first reading by about four tenths of a second each time you opened a page.
Every SIM Config switch now waits for the device to confirm the change and reads the value back. A setting the modem refuses reports why instead of quietly showing itself as on.
Applying a setting no longer runs on the interface thread, so the app stays responsive and cannot hang while a root or Shizuku write is in progress.
Rotating the phone or switching between light and dark no longer discards the SIM Config page or interrupts a change that is still being applied.
Controls are grouped into Network, Calling, and Status bar sections instead of one long list, and each one shows when it is applying.
The page reads the carrier configuration once rather than around thirty times, and no longer scans every configuration field it never used.
Every SIM Config control was rewritten in this release. Open SIM Config once after updating and confirm your VoLTE, VoNR, and band choices still read correctly.
Code shrinking is now enabled and fourteen unused libraries have been removed, cutting the release package from about 54 MB to roughly 3 MB.
This release is internal housekeeping only. Root and Shizuku behaviour, band selection, the modem patch, and field test are all unchanged.
Every change is now compiled and unit tested automatically before release, so build regressions are caught earlier.
Root SIM Config choices now stay together instead of later VoNR, VoWiFi, or enhanced-data-icon changes replacing earlier choices.
The app saves one complete profile per SIM and restores it after reboot, user unlock, app update, or Root service reconnect.
Restore Google defaults also removes the saved Root profile. Shizuku controls remain session-only and may reset after reboot.
Root mode can now show a live boxed VoLTE badge in Android’s right-side status area while IMS is registered over LTE or NR. The icon disappears when cellular IMS disconnects.
A separate right-side VoWiFi icon appears only when IMS is genuinely registered through IWLAN. These indicators do not create an ongoing notification.
A reversible per-SIM repair opens the Android WFC gates, selects Wi-Fi preferred, restarts IMS, and reports carrier ePDG, profile, DNS, or authentication blockers honestly.
Field reports now include the effective VoWiFi setting, IMS registration transport, IWLAN state, Wi-Fi state, and sanitized recent failure evidence.
This release focuses on VoLTE and VoWiFi visibility and diagnostics. It does not change the regional 5G modem patch or bypass carrier IMS provisioning.
The in-app guide now starts with dedicated, step-by-step Root and Shizuku 5G setup paths using the exact controls users need.
The guide covers Root Force, the Magisk regional modem compatibility patch, the required reboot, NSA-first testing, and firmware-update recovery.
Shizuku users get a separate Automatic-bands, Force NSA, Easy Mode, regional-profile, Monitor, and Field Test sequence.
Shizuku can open Android-side gates but cannot replace Tensor cfg.db. A modem-policy rejection can still require the Root/Magisk patch.
OTA updates now open a versioned liquid-glass What’s New screen. It preserves GitHub release notes across Android’s installer and can be reopened from About.
A calmer hierarchy, semantic status colors, refined typography, compact expert controls, glass surfaces and restrained motion now scale cleanly across Pixel displays.
The bottom bar is now custom-built with equal cells, fixed centered icon slots and stable label baselines. The app header also carries the by Nirmala signature.
Monitor and Field Test temporarily disable Wi-Fi, fail closed if isolation cannot be confirmed, and restore the previous Wi-Fi state when the session ends.
Reports now identify the OS build, operational PLMN, evidence source, NR and EN-DC flag semantics, IMS/callback coverage, readable policy gates and sanitized root modem deltas.
Every Pixel using Shizuku receives the regional 5G limitation notice on stock Pixel OS and supported alternative Pixel operating systems.
